subject: AtlasMed Q4 retro true-up invoice and rollforward plan
messages:
From: Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@atlasmed.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Retro usage Q4 2026 - makeup and next steps

Hi Karthik and team,

Quick note on our Q4 consumption that we flagged during renewal: our platform telemetry and your usage report show a 38% overage relative to the committed capacity for Nov-Dec 2026. Attached is our internal breakdown (AtlasMed_Q42026_usage_breakdown.xlsx) with per-environment peaks and the correlated API call windows.

We would like to close this out ahead of the renewal. Can you confirm the total one-time charge you plan to issue and whether we can amortize over the new 12-month commitment vs. a single invoice? Also, Samir asked if there is any goodwill credit available given the burst coincided with your endpoint migration on 2026-11-15.

Thanks,
Julia Stevens
Director of Finance, AtlasMed
billing@atlasmed.com

---
Attachments: AtlasMed_Q42026_usage_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42 KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retro usage Q4 2026 - makeup and next steps

Hi Julia,

Thanks for the breakdown — I reviewed the attached spreadsheet and cross-checked our server-side ingest logs. You are right: there's a clear spike in the Nov 12-18 window that pushed the monthly bill past the committed tier.

Options we can offer:
- One-time invoice for the delta (calculated as excess token-units) with an optional 20% courtesy credit tied to the fact the spike overlapped with our migration week.
- Amortize the net delta across the next 12 months and reduce the immediate payment burden.
- Convert part of the overage into a short-term capacity top-up at a discounted rate and apply remainder as a one-time invoice.

To give you a concrete number, the raw delta is $48,760. If we apply a 20% courtesy credit, the invoice amount would be $39,008. If you prefer amortization, we can roll $48,760 into the 12-month term at a 10% discount on unit pricing, and reflect that in an amendment to the MOPA.

Marissa — can you confirm if finance is comfortable issuing a 20% credit here? Ben — can you confirm ops/legal ok to create the invoice + amendment flow?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0184

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Julia Stevens <julia.stevens@atlasmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retro usage Q4 2026 - makeup and next steps

Hi all,

Reviewed on our side. A few notes:
- Finance is willing to extend a 20% courtesy credit for the one-time overage invoice given the migration context, provided AtlasMed signs the accompanying MOPA amendment that locks in the extended commit (6 months additional) and a minimum monthly baseline.
- If AtlasMed prefers amortization, we will need a signed amendment that includes the amortization schedule and an updated payment SOW. Our preference is to tie the amortization to the renewed commitment to avoid repeat bursts.

Karthik, I drafted a proposed one-time invoice PDF and a short amendment (Signed_MOPA_Amendment_draft.docx) — attaching for their review. Julia, if you can confirm which path you prefer by EOD Friday we can route the DocuSign for signatures and issue the invoice.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments: Proposed_OneTime_Invoice_0310.pdf, Signed_MOPA_Amendment_draft.docx

Date: Wed, 24 Feb 2027 08:56:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Retro usage Q4 2026 - makeup and next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the quick look.

AtlasMed leans toward amortizing over the next 12 months to smooth cashflow. That said, Samir wants a modest upfront payment to ensure commitment alignment. Proposal: 40% upfront, 60% amortized across 12 months. We are OK to sign the MOPA amendment with the 6-month extension and baseline as long as the amendment reflects the amortization schedule and the agreed 20% courtesy credit on the one-time delta.

Can Redwood confirm the exact monthly amortization line item and send us the DocuSign link? We need to get this into our March billing run.

Julia

Julia, Karthik —

Finance has approved the amortize + upfront structure. Final numbers below:
- Gross delta: $48,760
- 20% courtesy credit applied to gross delta: -$9,752
- Net balance to amortize: $39,008
- Upfront payment (40%): $15,603.20
- Remaining (60%): $23,404.80 to be spread over 12 months = $1,950.40/month (starting April invoice)

We'll generate the amortized line item on your monthly invoice and issue an initial one-time charge for the upfront amount once the amendment is signed. I've attached the finalized invoice PDF for your records. DocuSign link will follow from Marissa to get the MOPA amendment signed; please confirm the signer for AtlasMed.
